source.title: Multilingual Blending: Large Language Model Safety Alignment Evaluation with Language Mixture
source.authors: Jia-Yang Song; Yu-Heng Huang; Zhehua Zhou; Lei Ma

record.tranche_reason: The study reports harmful-response rates for multilingual blended prompts, but does not test fine-tuning, first-token KL concentration, compliant prefills, suffixes, decoding changes, safety-localized parameters, why safety is shallow, or deepening safety training.
record.gate_note: The reported bypass rates measure harmful compliance under multilingual blending, a different intervention from those named in V1–V7. They are recorded under fits_no_version rather than linked to a claim version. The first-token uncertainty analysis measures entropy, not aligned-versus-base per-token KL.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates a prompt-level multilingual-mixing jailbreak (mixed-language queries plus an instruction to answer in mixed languages). It uses no fine-tuning, no compliant-prefill, suffix or decoding manipulation, no per-token KL against a base model, no parameter localization and no deepening training. Its first-token measure is Shannon entropy of the aligned model's own distribution, not aligned-versus-base KL by position. Its only contact with the claim's sources is citing Qi et al. 2023 as an example of supervised fine-tuning for alignment. None of its results bear on V1–V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that mixed-language queries and responses (Multilingual Blending) bypass safety alignment of GPT-3.5, GPT-4o and five open models more often than single-language prompts. Resource level, number of languages, morphology and language family affect the rate. Elevated first-token uncertainty suggests the models are confused by mixed-language input.
record.recipe_differences: No fine-tuning, token-prefill, suffix, or decoding recipe from the named original sources is tested; the study evaluates multilingual blending as a prompt-and-response attack.
record.method_sensitivity: Bypass rates vary with query/response format, language combination and model. The authors report that the number of mixed languages affects rates, with around four often yielding higher rates; combinations with more than five languages sometimes lead GPT-3.5 to translate instead of answering.

fits_no_version.finding: Mixed-language queries combined with mixed-language responses raise Perspective-API-flagged unsafe-response rates well above single-language baselines. For GPT-4o, English is 0% and mixed combinations reach up to 40.34%. The same pattern appears on Llama3, Mixtral and Qwen1.5, and rates vary with language resource level, morphology, language family and number of languages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multilingual code-mixed prompting bypasses safety alignment, and its effectiveness depends on the language mixture and the model.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 6: first-token entropy is higher for bypassed than for safe responses, and higher under mixed-language prompts than single-language prompts. For example, GPT-3.5 safe English 0.11 vs mixed 1.13–1.41. No row records this table.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Higher first-token uncertainty accompanies safety-alignment failure under multilingual blending.

record.peer_reviewed: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: NAACL 2025
record.problems: The main evaluation uses Perspective API as an external safety judge; outputs are translated back to English for evaluation. Only 120 malicious prompts are selected. The text reports no uncertainty intervals or significance tests for the bypass rates. The authors note that Llama3-8B cannot follow the mixed-language response instruction, limiting interpretation of its mixed-condition rates.
record.rows_left_out: The 60-row limit required selection. Omitted remaining Table 2 combinations and Tables 1, 3, 4, and 5 bypass-rate entries, plus Table 6 first-token uncertainty entries; the retained rows prioritize query/response ablations (Appendix B, Table 7), model generalizability (Appendix H, Table 9), and selected number-of-language conditions (Table 2).

untested.parts: No aligned-versus-base per-token KL across response positions; Table 6 reports first-token entropy only.
No prefilled compliant opening, adversarial suffix or decoding change. The mixed-language response instruction is a prompt-format attack, not a manipulation of the opening tokens.
No test of the data or the objective as a cause of shallowness. The authors attribute bypass to English-centred alignment, but test no causal mechanism.
No deepening training or durability test.

record.verdict_notes: The relation changes from 'discusses' to 'cites_only': the paper never discusses shallow or first-token safety alignment and only cites Qi et al. 2023 in passing. All row links stay 'none'. The study selected 120 prompts, judged by Perspective API on back-translated outputs at a 0.3 threshold, which measures toxicity rather than harmful compliance. Llama3-8B could not produce mixed-language output, so its mixed-condition rows (r28–r30) are hard to interpret.

versions.untested_parts: No fine-tuning on harmful examples or measurement of its effect.
No benign-data fine-tuning or measurement of its effect.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement across response positions.
No compliant-start prefilling, adversarial suffix, or decoding-change test.
No weight or rank localization test.
No test of training data or objective as a cause of shallowness.
No training intended to deepen safety or test of its durability.

relation.reason: Qi et al. (2023) is cited as background on supervised fine-tuning and safety alignment; the study does not test or use its finding about safety erosion through fine-tuning.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates multilingual prompt and response formats, without testing or using any of V1–V7. First-token entropy does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL or its concentration across response positions.

source_check.notes: Bypass rates measure outputs flagged unsafe by Perspective API after English back-translation. Appendix H reports that Llama3-8B answered only in English despite mixed-language output instructions.
